name: National Scenic Areas
description: Scotland's 40 National Scenic Areas — the Scottish equivalent of National Landscapes, protecting remote mountains, lochs, islands, and coastlines of exceptional scenic value.

places.name: Assynt-Coigach
places.description: A dramatic Highland landscape of isolated, distinctively shaped mountains rising from ancient bog and lochan-studded moorland in northwest Sutherland.

places.name: Ben Nevis and Glen Coe
places.description: Home to the UK's highest peak and one of Scotland's most iconic and dramatic glens, scarred by the 1692 Massacre of Glencoe.

places.name: Cairngorm Mountains
places.description: A sub-arctic plateau landscape at the heart of the Cairngorms National Park, Britain's largest area of land over 1,000 metres.

places.name: Cuillin Hills
places.description: The jagged, near-vertical peaks of the Black Cuillin on Skye, widely regarded as the most challenging mountain terrain in the British Isles.

places.name: Deeside and Lochnagar
places.description: Royal Deeside's valley and the mountain of Lochnagar, long favoured by the Royal Family and the subject of a children's book written by King Charles III.

places.name: Dornoch Firth
places.description: A sheltered estuary in the Highlands known for dolphin sightings, sandy beaches, and the golf links of Royal Dornoch.

places.name: East Stewartry Coast
places.description: A rocky, indented coastline in Dumfries and Galloway around Kirkcudbright, an artists' town long known as the 'Scottish St Ives.'

places.name: Eildon and Leaderfoot
places.description: Three distinctive volcanic peaks in the Scottish Borders near Melrose, associated with legends of King Arthur and the wizard Michael Scot.

places.name: Fleet Valley
places.description: A wooded estuary landscape in Dumfries and Galloway around Gatehouse of Fleet, mixing woodland, farmland, and tidal mudflats.

places.name: Glen Affric
places.description: Often called the most beautiful glen in Scotland, home to remnants of the ancient Caledonian pine forest and a chain of lochs.

places.name: Glen Strathfarrar
places.description: A remote, access-restricted glen in the Highlands with a gated road, kept quiet and undeveloped, home to red deer and golden eagles.

places.name: Hoy and West Mainland
places.description: Orkney's most mountainous island, home to the Old Man of Hoy sea stack and dramatic cliffs including the UK's highest vertical rock face.

places.name: Jura
places.description: A sparsely populated Hebridean island dominated by the three conical Paps of Jura, where George Orwell wrote 1984.

places.name: Kintail
places.description: A range of dramatic peaks in the western Highlands including the Five Sisters of Kintail, a classic ridge-walking destination.

places.name: Knapdale
places.description: A quiet peninsula in Argyll between Loch Fyne and the Sound of Jura, notable as the site of Scotland's beaver reintroduction trial.

places.name: Knoydart
places.description: Mainland Britain's most remote community, accessible only by boat or a long hike, nicknamed 'the last wilderness.'

places.name: Kyle of Tongue
places.description: A sea loch on Scotland's remote north coast, part of the North Coast 500 route, overlooked by the peak of Ben Loyal.

places.name: Kyles of Bute
places.description: The narrow, sheltered sea channels separating the Isle of Bute from Argyll's Cowal peninsula, a popular sailing and sea-kayaking route.

places.name: Loch Lomond
places.description: Britain's largest lake by surface area, its bonnie banks made famous in Scotland's best-known folk song.

places.name: Loch na Keal (Isle of Mull)
places.description: A sea loch on Mull's west coast known as one of the best places in Britain to spot white-tailed sea eagles.

places.name: Loch Rannoch and Glen Lyon
places.description: A remote Highland Perthshire landscape of loch, forest, and Scotland's longest enclosed glen, overlooked by the Munro Schiehallion.

places.name: Loch Shiel
places.description: A long, narrow freshwater loch in the western Highlands, familiar to Harry Potter fans as the on-screen 'Black Lake' near Hogwarts.

places.name: Loch Tummel
places.description: A Perthshire loch famous for the 'Queen's View' viewpoint, reputedly named for Queen Victoria's visit in 1866.

places.name: Lynn of Lorn
places.description: A stretch of sheltered sea and islands near Oban on Scotland's west coast, a gateway to the Inner Hebrides.

places.name: Morar, Moidart and Ardnamurchan
places.description: Mainland Britain's westernmost point, a rugged coastal peninsula of white-sand beaches, single-track roads, and abundant wildlife.

places.name: North Arran
places.description: The mountainous northern half of the Isle of Arran, dominated by Goatfell, whose granite peaks have earned Arran the nickname 'Scotland in Miniature.'

places.name: Nith Estuary
places.description: The tidal mouth of the River Nith in Dumfries and Galloway, an important wintering site for migratory wildfowl.

places.name: North West Sutherland
places.description: One of Europe's last true wildernesses, an ancient landscape of isolated mountains and lochans on some of the world's oldest exposed rock.

places.name: River Earn (Comrie to St Fillans)
places.description: A gentle Perthshire river valley running from Comrie, a village once nicknamed 'Scotland's earthquake capital' for its seismic activity, to Loch Earn.

places.name: River Tay (Dunkeld)
places.description: A wooded stretch of Scotland's longest river around the cathedral town of Dunkeld, framed by the Hermitage's dramatic waterfall gorge.

places.name: Scarba, Lunga and the Garvellachs
places.description: A cluster of remote, largely uninhabited islands in the Firth of Lorn, close to the Corryvreckan whirlpool, one of the world's largest tidal whirlpools.

places.name: Shetland
places.description: Britain's northernmost island group, closer to Norway than Edinburgh, known for dramatic sea cliffs, puffin colonies, and Viking heritage.

places.name: Small Isles
places.description: Four small Hebridean islands — Eigg, Rum, Muck, and Canna — known for dramatic geology, wildlife, and tiny, tight-knit communities.

places.name: South Lewis, Harris and North Uist
places.description: A vast, scenically extreme stretch of the Outer Hebrides, spanning Harris's mountains and the white sands of Luskentyre beach.

places.name: South Uist Machair
places.description: A low-lying coastal strip of flower-rich grassland (machair) unique to the Scottish and Irish Atlantic coasts, vital for breeding wading birds.

places.name: St Kilda
places.description: A remote archipelago 40 miles into the Atlantic, a dual UNESCO World Heritage Site for both nature and culture, abandoned by its last residents in 1930.

places.name: The Trossachs
places.description: Often called the 'Highlands in miniature,' a compact landscape of lochs and wooded hills that inspired Sir Walter Scott's poetry.

places.name: Trotternish
places.description: Skye's northernmost peninsula, home to the otherworldly rock formations of the Quiraing and the Old Man of Storr.

places.name: Upper Tweeddale
places.description: The upland source of the River Tweed in the Scottish Borders, a landscape of rounded hills and remote farming valleys.

places.name: Wester Ross
places.description: One of Scotland's most celebrated wild landscapes, home to Torridon's ancient sandstone peaks among the oldest rock formations on Earth.
